Chapter 1: Basic Rules

Ability Checks

An ability check tests a creature’s innate talent against a task — whether Zoë the scout is climbing a cliff, forcing open a stuck door, or recalling a bit of half-remembered lore.

The Dungeon Master calls for an ability check when a character or monster attempts something with a real chance of failure. Success is never guaranteed — that is what makes the roll worth making.

  • Climbing a slick cliff face
  • Forcing open a stuck, locked, or barred door
  • Recalling useful information about local history

Advantage and Disadvantage

Sometimes circumstances tilt a roll in a character’s favor, and sometimes against it. The game handles both with the same simple tool.

Rolling with Advantage

  1. Roll two twenty-sided dice instead of one.
  2. Keep the higher of the two results.
  3. Add any other modifiers as normal.

OPTIONAL RULE: STACKING ADVANTAGE

Advantage and disadvantage never stack. If a roll would have advantage from several sources, or disadvantage from several sources, it is still only ever one extra die — never two.

Movement

A creature’s speed measures how far it can move during its turn.

Difficult Terrain

Zoë’s “careful step” trick does nothing here — every foot of movement in difficult terrain costs an extra foot.

Squeezing

A creature can squeeze through a space too small for it, but doing so costs extra movement and imposes disadvantage on attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws until it stops squeezing.
